evals.name: find-release-deployments
evals.prompt: Where is checkout v0.4.2 currently deployed? I need to know which spaces/environments have that release.
evals.expected_output: Uses `cub unit list` with where-data or read-only `cub function get ... get-container-image` to identify desired-state candidates containing :v0.4.2 and reports Unit/Space pairs without calling them currently deployed. For an actual deployment claim it routes those candidates to verify-apply for immutable Release/ManifestDigest, controller, and Kubernetes runtime evidence. Offers verified navigation and does not mutate.

evals.name: audit-missing-resource-limits
evals.prompt: Audit: find every Deployment across all our spaces where any container is missing resource requests or limits. I want to know the scope before I fix them.
evals.expected_output: Constructs a query (using --where-data or a CEL-based get-cel / vet-cel) that identifies Deployments whose containers lack resources.requests or resources.limits. Reports counts and specific unit/space pairs. Recommends `set-container-resources-defaults` via cub-mutate as the follow-up but does not run it.

evals.name: recent-changes-and-why
evals.prompt: What got changed in the myapp-prod space in the last 48 hours, and why? I'm trying to understand an alert.
evals.expected_output: Runs `cub revision list --space myapp-prod` filtered by UpdatedAt, surfaces the revisions with their --change-desc values (which include the user prompt and clarifications recorded at mutation time), and summarizes the changes in plain English. Offers the GUI revision-list link.

evals.name: single-unit-image-lookup
evals.prompt: What image tag is our nonprod worker running?
evals.expected_output: Locates the Space and Unit via `cub space list` and `cub unit list --space <space>` without guessing, then extracts the desired image with `cub unit data` or read-only `cub function get ... get-container-image`. Labels it desired ConfigHub state, not the currently running image. Because the prompt asks what is running, routes to verify-apply for Release/controller/Kubernetes proof; does not mutate.

evals.name: single-workload-replica-count-in-region
evals.prompt: How many replicas does our frontend have in us-east?
evals.expected_output: Resolves the workload/region phrasing by listing Spaces (matching a slug only when evidenced, or a Space Label such as Region=us-east-2) and candidate Units without inventing identity. Uses read-only `cub function get ... get-replicas` or `cub unit data`, reports spec.replicas, keeps single-workload scope, and does not mutate. If layout is ambiguous, references confighub-core rather than guessing.

evals.name: single-unit-up-to-date-check
evals.prompt: Is our nonprod worker up to date with the latest confighub release?
evals.expected_output: Extracts the desired ConfigHub image reference from the Unit and labels it as desired, never currently running. Resolves the comparison reference from an authoritative release source, then routes through verify-apply to bind an immutable ConfigHub Release/ManifestDigest to controller and Kubernetes runtime evidence before declaring the worker up to date. Reports any missing evidence as a proof gap and does not mutate.
